MCP (any harness)

Any MCP client that speaks streamable HTTP can use the tools. One URL, no account, and no key to try the public tools.

On this page
  • Connect
  • Agent skill
  • What the server lists
  • Reading a result
  • Run it locally (stdio)
  • Limits
Ask on DiscordBack to top
Endpoint
https://data.example.test/v1/mcp
Transport
Streamable HTTP, stateless, JSON responses. One JSON-RPC 2.0 message per POST; GET and DELETE answer 405.
Auth
None to try the public tools (trial limits). Optional: X-Janice-Key for a Janice appraisal with appraise_items. A free API key for daily use and the keyed tool, sent as Authorization: Bearer ecd_... or X-API-Key: ecd_.... With Claude Code: add --header "X-API-Key: ecd_…" to the claude mcp add command.
Rate limit
20 requests per minute and 200 a day per client without a key; 120 per minute and 10,000 a day with one

Connect#

$ claude mcp add --transport http --scope user eve-cyno https://data.example.test/v1/mcp
# Customize > Connectors > Add custom connector. Paste this https://data.example.test/v1/mcp and choose “No sign-in”.
https://data.example.test/v1/mcp
# If the dialog shows “Request headers” and you have a key: add the header x-api-key, with the key as its value.
# Team and Enterprise: an owner adds it under Organization settings > Connectors.
# ~/.cursor/mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "eve-cyno": {
      "url": "https://data.example.test/v1/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-API-Key": "<your EVE-Cyno API key, optional>"
      }
    }
  }
}
// .vscode/mcp.json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "eve-cyno-key",
      "description": "EVE-Cyno API key (optional)",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "eve-cyno": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://data.example.test/v1/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-API-Key": "${input:eve-cyno-key}"
      }
    }
  }
}
$ codex mcp add eve-cyno --url https://data.example.test/v1/mcp
$ gemini mcp add -s user -t http eve-cyno https://data.example.test/v1/mcp
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "eve-cyno": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://data.example.test/v1/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-Janice-Key": "<your Janice key, optional>",
        "X-API-Key": "<your EVE-Cyno API key, optional>"
      }
    }
  }
}
Add to CursorOpens Cursor and installs eve-cyno, no key. Install in VS CodeOpens VS Code and installs eve-cyno, no key.

With an API key: Codex CLI takes --bearer-token-env-var EVE_CYNO_API_KEY (the endpoint accepts Authorization: Bearer; this is the only form that carries a key there), and Gemini CLI takes -H "X-API-Key: ecd_…". Gemini connects it once the folder is trusted.

claude.ai and Claude Desktop

Connector calls reach the server from Anthropic's published outbound IPv4 ranges, 160.79.104.0/21 and 153.61.208.0/20 (no outbound IPv6; source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/ip-addresses). When the server is at capacity it answers HTTP 503 with Retry-After: 1 (code busy), before any authentication error and never charged against a limit; retry after that many seconds. Without a key they share one limit per client with every other connector user. A free key gives you your own: see API keys.

The JSON is the shape the Claude Code plugin ships. Other clients name these fields their own way (Windsurf uses serverUrl; Zed takes url and may add headers): look for an HTTP or streamable-HTTP server setting and give it the URL.

In Claude Code, check it with claude mcp list (it shows eve-cyno as Connected; in a session, /mcp). --scope user makes the server available in every project; without it, it is saved for the current directory only. Remove it with claude mcp remove eve-cyno --scope user. In Claude Code the tools are named mcp__eve-cyno__<tool>; allow them all with mcp__eve-cyno__*.

More harnesses

Claude Code has a plugin that ships the server, a skill and commands. Every client above connects with the URL alone. If yours is missing, ask on the EVE-Cyno Discord.

Agent skill#

The eve-data skill tells an agent which tool to call when, and which attribution to keep. It works with the MCP server and, without MCP, over REST with curl.

Install the skill
$ mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills/eve-data && curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eve-cyno/claude-plugins/main/plugins/eve-cyno/skills/eve-data/SKILL.md -o ~/.agents/skills/eve-data/SKILL.md

Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and VS Code read ~/.agents/skills. Claude Code reads ~/.claude/skills/eve-data/ instead: put the file there, or install the plugin, which ships the skill.

What the server lists#

tools/list follows the access tiers and is chosen per request:

TierIn tools/list
publicAlways.
keyedOnly when the caller presents a valid API key.
disabledNever. Calling one is the protocol's own "unknown tool" error.

Reading a result#

content[0]
The text answer, exactly as REST returns it in result.text.
content[1]
A short "Sources:" line, when the tool has upstreams. Most clients do not show _meta to the model, and attribution is a condition of several licences.
structuredContent
The typed result (REST: result.data).
_meta
The attribution.

Run it locally (stdio)#

The cmd/mcp binary of this module speaks MCP over stdio, for Claude Desktop, Claude Code and other stdio hosts. It reads the SDE from EVE_CORE_SDE_PATH.

core module
$ go run ./cmd/mcp

Limits#

20 requests per minute and 200 a day per client without a key, or 120 per minute and 10,000 a day with an API key. A session is a handful of requests (the handshake is three) plus one per tool call. The live tools have one limit of their own, 5 calls per minute per caller without a key and 10 with one, shared with REST. Request bodies are capped at 64 KiB.
